rationale: M60-C (#921) — the C half, and it is an INVARIANT pin rather than a defect reproduction, deliberately. #921's rule is that a `contains` edge carries the line that NAMES the child; in this analyzer the two candidate lines already coincide for the shapes that matter, because the struct/union member extractor ranges the field at its DECLARATOR (`rawDecl`, the loop that skips `primitive_type`/`type_identifier`/`type_qualifier`/`struct_specifier`/… and stops at `field_identifier`/`identifier`), not at the whole field_declaration — so `unsigned long long` on one line and the name on the next still yields a symbol whose range starts on the NAME's line. The `meta.nameLine` field the rule is keyed on is therefore equal to `range.startLine` in every row this fixture produces (measured: counter 16/16, oneline 17/17, byte_value 23/23, word_value 25/25, options 32/32, plain 33/33, bits 31/31), and an expectation with FORBID entries for the declaration-start line would be self-contradictory. What this fixture therefore does is pin the invariant the rule depends on — member containment lands on the member's own name line in C — so that a change to the C member extractor's range (the plausible way this could regress) is caught rather than assumed. NO C MUTANT ACCOMPANIES IT, and that is the honest reason: the pre-fix C behaviour is byte-identical on this fixture, so a mutant reproducing it would SURVIVE and prove nothing — the same measurement that retired `cpp/metadata-only-line-second-base`. The residue #921 was filed for is real and is measured on the cpp fixture beside this one: of the oracle's 166 rows, the 101 it attributes to lane `c` are produced by the CPP analyzer, on .h files that lane draws and the product dispatches to cpp by the language-detection policy (verified per file: every one of those rows comes back from `parseFile` with `language: "cpp"`).

expectSymbols.name: bits
expectSymbols.note: #951: the owner was `anonymous_struct` until this wave, which is a file-global PLACEHOLDER -- every anonymous struct in a file collapsed onto it, so two members of two different anonymous types looked like one type's duplicate member. The corpus census reported exactly that for curl's ftplistparser.c (`anonymous_struct.main x2`), and the lane's own P8 property called it a violation when another fixture grew five inline aggregates. The owner is now the MEMBER PATH, `Outer.options`, which is derived from the source and is unique by construction. This fixture's own note previously said the synthesised name 'is written nowhere' -- it now is.

the union spelling of the wrapped-type member
